messages:
Anya: FYI customer AcmeHealth just escalated — they rotated a service API key last night and since ~02:00 UTC some backend jobs are getting 403s while others keep succeeding. They report a mix of successes/failures, looks intermittent.
Mohit: Can you drop the original request/response (no PII) and which key id was rotated?
Anya: Key id: sk_live_ace42. Repro log from their failing job: ```
POST /v1/generate 403 
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d"
}
Headers: X-API-Key: sk_live_ace42, X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
```
Mohit: Thanks. Have we confirmed the rotation flow completed in Vault/KMS and that the old key was marked revoked?
Anya: Support verified in Vault UI that the old secret action=revoked at 01:45 UTC and new key bound to AcmeHealth. The customer says some long-running jobs (cron workers) still using the old secret.
Lee: Quick suspicion: we recently rolled out an envoy auth plugin change that caches successful key validations at the edge for 10m to reduce auth RPCs. If some mesh nodes had the old key cached and others did not, that explains the mixed behavior.
Mohit: Oh — we also have the sidecar that does a KMS unwrap once and stores unwrapped credential in memory for the process lifetime. If the job keeps using the old environment var value (old key) but the sidecar had previously unwrapped it and cached success, that could allow it to continue until pod restart.
Sara: Customer indicated some jobs restarted after 03:30 and then started failing consistently — consistent with cache TTL + restarts.
Anya: I can repro locally against staging:
```bash
# old key passes or fails depending on node cache state
curl -H "X-API-Key: sk_live_ace42" -i https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# returns either 200 or 403 depending on which sidecar/node handles it
```
Mohit: Can you grab edge-proxy logs around req_0a1b2c3d? Look for auth cache hits vs auth service calls.
Anya: Pasted logs: ```
[edge-01] 2026-11-12T01:58:23Z req_0a1b2c3d auth: cache_miss -> forward to auth-svc
[edge-01] 2026-11-12T01:58:24Z auth-svc reply: 403 invalid_api_key
[edge-02] 2026-11-12T01:59:10Z req_0a1b2c5f auth: cache_hit (key:sk_live_ace42) -> allow
```
Anya: So exactly — some nodes had cache_hit.
Lee: That confirms it. The cache invalidation path is broken when Vault marks a key revoked because we rely on a pub/sub notification to the control plane. There was a hole where deprovision events from our Vault sync missed the pubsub publish if Vault responded with 202 (accept) vs 200. We changed that sync code 2 weeks ago.
Mohit: Ok root cause: race between Vault revocation path and our envoy auth cache invalidation (pubsub publish sometimes skipped). Impact: transient acceptance of revoked keys on nodes with a warm cache.
Sara: Customer-facing mitigation?
Anya: I asked them to restart the affected worker pods (quick fix) and they reported errors cleared for those after restart. I also forced a cache flush on our staging edge via admin endpoint.
Mohit: For prod mitigation we can: 1) trigger a manual cache flush for edge mesh (admin bulk endpoint) 2) temporarily set envoy auth cache TTL to 0 while we patch the sync, 3) provide customer with a short window to rotate again after confirm.
Lee: Commands I ran to flush caches from eng-sre: ```bash
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/edge-control -- curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/admin/cache/keys/flush -d '{"key":"sk_live_ace42"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
# or bulk flush
curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/admin/cache/keys/flush-all
```
Mohit: Action items: - eng-runtime: revert/patch Vault sync to always publish revocation event on all non-4xx responses (MOHIT-142) - eng-sre: add an automated invalidation job after rotation that calls admin endpoint (LEE-93) - devex/support: update rotation runbook to instruct customers to restart pods if they run long-lived processes (SARA-77)
Anya: I've opened a support ticket with AcmeHealth and told them we're doing a cache flush and patching the sync; they are ok with planned maintenance window tonight.
rot-deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/edge-auth-plugin v3.1.2 -> 6 pods, strategy=rolling
Lee: Patch is going out for the Vault sync in canary now. Once canary is healthy we'll set TTL back to 10m. We should also add a revocation webhook so Vault -> control plane is synchronous for revokes.
Mohit: Also adding metrics: revocation_event_publish_failures and auth_cache_invalidation_lag. Will file follow-ups.
Sara: I'll update the runbook and notify customer success to follow up post-maintenance.
Anya: Closing the thread once prod flush + patch done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
